reasons: Missing-status claim is well supported: the cited paragraphs show the Agreement presupposes an indemnity (9.3 cross-refers to 'Section 20.5', 21.3 excludes 'indemnification obligations' from the cap, 19.5 preserves an 'indemnity'), yet no such section exists — a critical gap under INDEMN.

Redline is inserted at the correct location (immediately after Section 19.5, before Limitation of Liability) and its five paragraphs map cleanly to 20.1–20.5, curing the dangling 9.3 reference to Section 20.5 as claimed.

Rule coverage is complete and directionally correct for the customer: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies; and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, matching the preferred position with fallback exclusions as a stated concession.

Additions beyond model language (bodily injury/property damage, fraud, 'Customer has no other indemnification obligation') are pro-customer, market-standard, and do not render the edit non-minimal; deterministic checks all pass.
Comment carries the [Playbook] prefix, uses first person plural, explains the change and cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback on IP exclusions.

Minor (non-blocking) cleanup: the inserted paragraphs render without clause numbers while internally citing 'Section 20.1(a)' and 'Section 20.1', and 'Vendor Technology' / 'Affiliates' are used without confirmed definitions — worth aligning numbering and defined terms before sending.
